docs.title: Hand-off checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Every transaction has an explicit group/code.
  • [ ] Tables/columns are named; DDL is included if they don't exist yet.
  • [ ] Schema SQL comes first and is marked "Execute".
  • [ ] Transactions are single-purpose and wired together.
  • [ ] The plan is phased into approval-sized batches.
  • [ ] Durable rules are separated out for AGENTS.md.
  • [ ] No step assumes the builder can delete, deploy, or run SQL itself.

Feeding the plan to the builder: paste the durable conventions into the project's AGENTS.md once; paste the data model + transactions into the agent chat phase by phase, approving each batch before moving on.

docs.title: Application security reference
docs.text: This guide describes authentication and authorization for one-shot generated SOAD applications. It is intended for application developers, deployers, and operators.

docs.title: Architecture and production boundary
docs.text:
app/s0adm/ is the online IDE and control plane. It is not an authentication service for deployed applications and must not be included in production images.

Generated applications use one of these modes:

Mode Identity source When to use it local The application's own datasource and the framework auth runtime Protected applications; this is the default custom An application transaction implementing the provider interface SSO, OIDC, an existing account system, or another replacement public No identity provider Applications whose security profile is entirely public

In local mode the framework supplies login/logout, password reset, invitations, TOTP, profiles, session revocation, user administration, CSRF protection, and role/permission enforcement. Its routes are under /_soad/auth/*; it does not import or query s0adm.

IDE sessions use keys such as s0uid. Application sessions use distinct soad.auth.* keys and a revocable record in the application database. An IDE login is therefore never accepted as an application login.

docs.title: Generation defaults
docs.text:
One-shot generation infers a security profile from the business requirements:

Application Profile and mode CRM, ERP, HR, invoicing, internal CRUD, dashboards, private/customer data authenticated + local Landing pages, documentation, brochure sites, genuinely public catalogs public + public Public content plus staff/customer workflows mixed + local Ambiguous brief authenticated + local

Operators can disable this inference with:

ai.one.shot.auto.security = false

The equivalent environment variable is ai_one_shot_auto_security=false. When disabled, one-shot generation uses public access without a login unless the product prompt explicitly requests authentication or access control. Explicit requests for login, private or protected access, accounts, roles, or permissions still produce the appropriate authenticated security plan. The default is true; restart the IDE after changing the property or environment variable.

Local registration is invite_only unless the brief explicitly requires open registration. Open registration requires a least-privilege member role, which is granted to new accounts; it never grants admin. The generator does not create login, password, session, user, or ACL code inside business transactions.

The accepted plan produces:

  • WEB-INF/security/app-security.json, the immutable runtime security manifest;
  • WEB-INF/deploy/auth-mysql.sql, the production installation bundle;
  • WEB-INF/deploy/auth-h2.sql, the development/test installation bundle.

These artifacts come from the same normalized plan. The SQL contains schema, roles, and permissions but never users, password verifiers, invitations, sessions, or other secrets.

docs.title: Manual setup (without one-shot generation)
docs.text:
An existing or hand-built app has no app-security.json until you configure one. Do this from the IDE, without the AI assistant:

  1. Open Settings → Application for the app.
  2. If the app has no security metadata yet, the Security card shows a profile/mode picker instead of the read-only summary. Choose:
  3. Security profile — public, authenticated, or mixed.
  4. Authentication mode — local (framework-managed users in the app's own database) or custom (your own provider transaction). public mode is only offered when the profile is also public.
  5. Authenticated and mixed profiles require at least one role. Enter it in the initial Roles editor:
admin|Administrator|Full access
member|Member

The example above expresses code, name, and description; enter these in the corresponding role row fields. Only the role code is required (lowercase, starts with a letter, e.g. [a-z][a-z0-9_.:-]*); name defaults to the code and description is optional. Leave the box empty for a public profile — public profiles must not declare roles. 4. Save. This validates the plan, writes the manifest and both SQL bundles, and — for local mode — installs the local-auth schema into the app's database immediately and grants your IDE account system_admin plus the first listed role. A one-time, 20-minute setup link to set your local password is shown on the page; do not share or log it.

Initial setup creates roles without business permission grants. After saving, open the application's Roles and permissions section to register permission codes and assign grants to roles. The editor audits controller policies and identifies missing permission codes. Save to publish the updated manifest and install matching development metadata. Do not confuse this editor with the platform's IDE Roles screen. The transaction-editor AI path below is another way to stage a complete security plan.

Switching auth_mode later (once a profile exists) uses the same Security card without re-entering roles — see Switching providers.

docs.title: Alternative: the per-transaction editor AI (superadmin only)
docs.text:
Besides the Settings form above and one-shot generation, a superadmin can also have the AI assistant propose a security plan while editing transactions in a normal (non-one-shot) chat session — including full roles and permissions:

  • The chat session exposes a stage_app_security tool only when session.security_management is true, which the server sets from is_superadmin(user_id) on every chat session (app/s0adm/ai/chat.py, set_security_management). Non-superadmins never see this tool; regular one-shot generation sessions reject it too — one-shot uses its own embedded plan instead.
  • Asking the assistant to set up or change roles/permissions/profile calls stage_app_security (app/s0adm/ai/tools.py, _stage_app_security), which builds and validates the manifest, checks that no already-assigned role would be orphaned, and audits every routed transaction's ACCESS_POLICY against the proposed plan — but only stages it. Nothing is written yet.
  • The staged plan appears in the normal diff/approval UI alongside any staged code changes. Approving it (app/s0adm/ai/chat.py, approve) re-checks that the approver is a superadmin, then calls the same security_mod.configure_app_security(...) used by the manual form — so the effect (manifest + SQL bundles written, local-auth schema installed, setup link issued) is identical either way.

Use this path when you want AI help drafting roles/permissions/rationale. The manual application Roles and permissions editor also supports those grants.

docs.title: Controller contract
docs.text:
Each routed controller method needs an exact ACCESS_POLICY entry:

class Contact(object):
    ACCESS_POLICY = {
        "view": "permission:contacts.read",
        "save": "permission:contacts.write",
    }

    def view(self, ctx):
        current_user = ctx.output.get("current_user")

    def save(self, ctx):
        """POST"""
        pass

Policy values are:

  • public;
  • authenticated;
  • permission:<manifest-permission-code>.

Use the provider-neutral template values:

{{#if current_user}}
  <span>{{current_user.full_name}}</span>
  <a href="{{logout_url}}">Sign out</a>
{{else}}
  <a href="{{login_url}}">Sign in</a>
{{/if}}

<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">

current_user is in ctx.output; it is not an attribute of ctx. Never use ctx.current_user or getattr(ctx, "current_user", None).

docs.title: Deploying local authentication
docs.text:
Only MySQL production databases and H2 development/test databases are supported initially. Generation and installation reject other dialects.

  1. Build the runtime base, which intentionally does not copy app/s0adm/:
docker build -f app/Dockerfile-base-runtime \
  -t your-registry/soad-runtime:VERSION app

  1. Build the generated application layer using app/Dockerfile-runtime and that base image.

  2. Extract or obtain WEB-INF/deploy/auth-mysql.sql from the generated workspace/image and apply it explicitly to the application database before rollout:

mysql --host DB_HOST --user DB_USER --password --database APP_DATABASE \
  < webapp/WEB-INF/deploy/auth-mysql.sql
  1. Configure the runtime datasource through environment variables:
db_default_url
db_default_driver_class
db_default_username
db_default_password
  1. Create the first application administrator with password input on stdin:
printf '%s\n' "$INITIAL_PASSWORD" |
  docker exec -i APPLICATION_CONTAINER \
    soad-auth-admin create-admin \
    --app default \
    --email admin@example.com \
    --name "Application Administrator" \
    --password-stdin

Prefer a secret-file/stdin mechanism that does not place the password in shell history. The CLI refuses password arguments, validates the manifest and installed schema checksum, and grants both system_admin and the generated owner/admin role.

  1. Check readiness:
GET /_soad/auth/health

It returns 200 only when the installed schema version and manifest checksum match the image. A protected route returns 503 instead of running unauthenticated when SQL has not been applied.

The production configuration is app/conf/sufia-runtime.properties. It contains the application transaction and auth servlets only. It has no db.s0adm, /s0adm/t/*, IDE listener, IDE static mapping, extra Jython path, file editor, database editor, AI endpoint, deployment screen, or log servlet.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
When one-shot generation publishes a protected application, the IDE explicitly installs the appropriate MySQL/H2 bundle into the development application database. It creates an application-local record matching the developer's email but does not copy the IDE password or trust the IDE session.

The authenticated generation completion includes a 20-minute, single-use setup URL. Opening it sets a separate local password. Do not publish this URL in logs, source control, chat history, or deployment artifacts.

docs.title: Built-in pages and administration
docs.text:
The local provider exposes:

Route Purpose /_soad/auth/login, /logout Session creation and revocation /_soad/auth/bootstrap Initial administrator setup when none is active /_soad/auth/register Open registration when enabled /_soad/auth/forgot, /reset Generic, single-use password recovery /_soad/auth/invite Invitation acceptance and initial password setup /_soad/auth/profile, /password Profile and password changes /_soad/auth/totp/setup Authenticator-app enrollment/removal /_soad/auth/sessions List and revoke active sessions /_soad/auth/admin/users Invite, enable/disable, and assign roles /_soad/auth/health Schema/manifest readiness

system_admin includes the reserved auth.users.manage permission. Generated business roles are separate. Disabling a user or resetting a password revokes their active sessions.

SMTP is optional for local development. When it is not configured, an administrator can copy the invitation link from the result page. Production password recovery requires mail configuration. Set sufia_hostname to the public HTTPS origin (for example, https://app.example.com) when the runtime is behind a reverse proxy so emailed links use the external address.

docs.title: Customizing built-in authentication pages
docs.text:
Local authentication supports validated Handlebars overrides under:

webapp/WEB-INF/auth-overrides/

The supported files are login.html, verify-totp.html, register.html, bootstrap.html, forgot.html, reset.html, invite.html, profile.html, sessions.html, totp-setup.html, admin-users.html, and error.html. A shared stylesheet may be placed at webapp/assets/auth-overrides/auth.css. Public mode has no login UI, and custom providers own their complete login flow.

Every page receives escaped common values including:

{{title}}
{{csrf_token}}
{{message}}
{{error}}
{{context_path}}
{{default_stylesheet_url}}
{{stylesheet_url}}

Page contexts also provide their action/navigation URLs and applicable token, user, role, TOTP, or session-list data. Existing login placeholders such as {{action_url}} and {{forgot_url}} remain supported.

admin-users additionally provides {{create_action_url}} for the add-user form, whose fields are full_name, email, the optional password and password_confirm, and a repeated role_codes checkbox per entry in {{roles}}. Leaving both password fields empty creates the account pending and issues a one-time setup link, returned as {{invite_link}}; each entry in {{users}} carries a pending flag for that state. These inputs are optional in an override — a template that omits them keeps validating, and simply does not offer the feature.

Overrides are limited to 128 KiB per HTML page and 256 KiB for the stylesheet. They must compile, retain the page's required form actions and input names, and render {{csrf_token}} for state-changing forms. Executable URLs, frames/objects, <base>, and unescaped triple-brace values are rejected on every screen. So is any URL pointing at another origin: an https://, http://, or //host value in href/xlink:href/src/action/formaction, or in an @import/url() in the stylesheet — no CDN stylesheet, remote image, font host, or off-site form target. Relative paths, {{context_path}}/…, #fragment, mailto:, and data: URIs of image or font types are unaffected. A missing or invalid file logs a warning and falls back to the framework page.

Script is allowed by screen, not globally:

  • The four signed-in management screens -- profile, sessions, totp-setup, admin-users -- accept an inline <script> and inline event handlers. They are reached only after _require_user (and, for admin-users, the auth.users.manage permission), so the reader is already authenticated, and these list-and-row pages want a modal or a disclosure toggle to be usable.
  • Every other screen is shown to an anonymous visitor and rejects both, because script there can read the password field and the CSRF token.
  • No screen accepts script from outside the application. <script src=...> and <script type="module"> (whose import can fetch remote code with no src) are rejected everywhere: a fetched script can change under the deployment, and it fails entirely in an air-gapped install.

The four relaxed routes also carry a Content-Security-Policy response header (script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', connect-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none') so the browser enforces the same in/out distinction on what a regex over the markup cannot see -- a remote import() or fetch() from inside a script body. The sign-in flow sends no CSP.

The transaction-editor AI stages these files through the normal diff and approval workflow. Deleting an override restores the framework default. An override changes presentation only; it never replaces credential verification, sessions, CSRF, roles, or permissions.

For different authentication behavior rather than different styling, use a custom provider.

docs.title: Changing the logo
docs.text:
The narrow, single-purpose screens (sign in, register, forgot, reset, invite, verify-2FA, error) show a small mark above the title. By default this is the framework's own SOAD icon; a developer can replace it by placing a bare, self-contained SVG at:

webapp/WEB-INF/auth-overrides/mark.svg

This is validated like the other overrides but is not a Handlebars template -- it is inlined as-is into the page, once per narrow screen, so it has its own, narrower rules:

  • The whole file must be a single <svg>...</svg> element: no XML declaration, <!DOCTYPE>, or entity, and nothing before/after the root tag.
  • No <script>, inline event handlers (onload, onclick, ...), frames, <object>/<embed>, or <foreignObject> (which can smuggle arbitrary HTML/script inside an SVG).
  • href/xlink:href may only point at a local #fragment (e.g. a <use> referencing a <symbol> defined earlier in the same file) -- no external file or data: URL, keeping the mark a single self-contained asset for air-gapped deployments, same as everything else this stylesheet ships.
  • Limited to 24 KiB.

Any class/aria-hidden attribute on the root <svg> is stripped and replaced by the framework (class="auth-mark" aria-hidden="true"), so sizing comes from the page's own CSS regardless of what the file declares -- set a viewBox and skip width/height on the root element and let the page size it. A missing or invalid mark.svg falls back to the framework mark, same as any other override. The transaction-editor AI can stage it too, via stage_auth_override with screen: "mark". Wide management screens (profile, sessions, 2FA, admin users) never show the mark, override or not.

docs.title: Switching providers
docs.text:
In the IDE, open Settings → Application and choose:

  • Application-local identity;
  • Custom application provider;
  • Public, available only for a public profile.

Saving the setting regenerates the manifest and both SQL bundles. Controllers and their ACCESS_POLICY declarations do not need to change.

docs.title: Custom provider interface
docs.text:
Set the module to a lowercase application transaction path such as security/auth_provider. Its class must implement:

class Auth_provider(object):
    def current_user(self, ctx):
        return None

    def authenticate(self, ctx):
        return None

    def authorize(self, ctx, action, permission):
        return False

    def validate_csrf(self, ctx):
        return False

    def login_url(self, ctx):
        return "%s/t/security/login" % ctx.ctxPath

    def logout_url(self, ctx):
        return "%s/t/security/login/logout" % ctx.ctxPath

The provider transaction itself is not routable through the transaction engine. Methods fail closed: protected actions require a non-null authenticated user, permission checks require exactly True, and protected mutations require exactly True from validate_csrf.

Switching to custom or public stops loading the built-in local provider. The reserved local tables may be left in place for an easy rollback or removed later through an operator-reviewed database migration; the runtime never drops them.

docs.title: Security behavior
docs.text:
• Passwords use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, a random per-user salt, 600,000 iterations, and stored algorithm/cost metadata.
  • Login attempts are rate-limited and responses do not disclose whether an account exists.
  • Reset/invitation tokens are random, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, expire, and are single-use.
  • Protected local mutations require CSRF validation; public business mutations must validate CSRF explicitly. Built-in auth forms validate their own tokens.
  • Return URLs must be same-application absolute paths.
  • Authentication rotates the HTTP session ID and CSRF token.
  • Runtime sessions are revocable database records, not merely browser session attributes.
  • The shipped production profile uses HttpOnly, SameSite=None, and Secure. The tracker deployment explicitly selects Lax for its same-site flow.

The runtime image build also fails when /app/s0adm exists or generated application source imports or links to s0adm. In a valid production image, /s0adm/* has no mapping and returns 404.

docs.title: Authentication override contract
docs.text:
Everything required to produce a drop-in replacement for the built-in authentication UI. A generator that follows this document can emit a folder that is copied into a deployed application and works without a restart.

This document is structure only — it defines filenames, required markup, available data, and the validator rules. All visual design (layout, palette, typography, spacing, component styling) is left to the generator.

Source of truth: app/server/auth/overrides.py (validator) and app/server/AuthServlet.py (context builder). See also application security.

docs.title: 1. Output layout
docs.text:
⚠️ Not every file goes into WEB-INF/auth-overrides/. The stylesheet must be web-reachable, so it lives under webapp/assets/. Emitting auth.css into WEB-INF/auth-overrides/ results in a silently unstyled page — the file is never read and never served.

Generate this tree, rooted at the application's webapp/ directory:

webapp/
├── WEB-INF/
│   └── auth-overrides/
│       ├── login.html
│       ├── verify-totp.html
│       ├── register.html
│       ├── bootstrap.html
│       ├── forgot.html
│       ├── reset.html
│       ├── invite.html
│       ├── profile.html
│       ├── sessions.html
│       ├── totp-setup.html
│       ├── admin-users.html
│       ├── error.html
│       └── mark.svg          (optional logo; NOT a template — see §8)
└── assets/
    └── auth-overrides/
        └── auth.css          (optional stylesheet — MUST be here, not WEB-INF)

Rules:

  • Every file is independently optional. A screen with no override file falls back to the framework page. A partial set is valid.
  • No other filenames are recognized. Extra files in the folder are ignored — there is no way to add a page, a second stylesheet, an image, or a font file. Everything a page needs must be in its own .html or in auth.css.
  • Files are read per request, not cached. Adding, editing, or deleting a file takes effect on the next page load. No restart, no rebuild. (Contrast with ActiveJDBC models, which do require a restart.)
  • UTF-8 only. Files are read as UTF-8; any other encoding makes the screen fall back.
  • Deleting a file restores the framework default.
  • Overrides apply only when the application's auth mode is local. public mode has no login UI; a custom provider owns its own flow.

Size limits (exceeding = rejected):

File Limit any .html 128 KiB auth.css 256 KiB mark.svg 24 KiB

docs.title: 2. Failure behavior — what "no error upon run" means
docs.text:
An invalid override never produces a 500 or a broken page. The framework:

  1. calls the validator on every render (not just at install time),
  2. on any failure, logs WARNING: Invalid authentication override <screen>,
  3. renders its own built-in page instead.

So the failure mode is silent reversion to the default look. If a generated page "does nothing", the file is being rejected — check the server log for the warning, which names the screen and the exact reason.

Because validation runs per request, keep pages lean; multi-hundred-KiB pages pay a regex + Handlebars compile on every hit.

docs.title: 3. Hard rules — any one of these rejects the file
docs.text:
The screens fall into two groups, and the script rules differ between them:

  • Pre-sign-in screens — login, verify-totp, register, bootstrap, forgot, reset, invite, error. Shown to an anonymous visitor, carrying the password field and the CSRF token. No JavaScript of any kind.
  • Signed-in management screens — profile, sessions, totp-setup, admin-users. Reached only after authentication (admin-users additionally requires the auth.users.manage permission). Inline JavaScript is allowed.

Rejected on every screen:

Rejected Use instead <script src="…"> — any external script, incl. a CDN tag inline <script> on a management screen; auth.css for styling <script type="module"> — its import can fetch remote code with no src a classic inline <script> <iframe>, <frame>, <frameset>, <object>, <embed>, <applet> plain HTML elements href/xlink:href/src/action/formaction starting javascript:, vbscript:, data:text/html a normal path The same attributes starting https://, http://, or //host — a CDN stylesheet, a remote image, a font host, an off-site form target, an outbound <a> a path on this application; embed an image or font as a data: URI <base> — it silently re-points every relative URL, including the form carrying the password nothing; the URLs you need are in the page context <meta http-equiv="refresh"> let the server redirect {{{value}}} or {{&value}} (unescaped output) {{value}} — always escaped

A data: URI of an image or font type is fine, and so are mailto: and tel: — none of them fetches from another origin. {{stylesheet_url}}, {{context_path}}/…, #fragment, and any relative path are unaffected.

Rejected on the pre-sign-in screens only:

Rejected Use instead <script> in any form, including inline auth.css — it is linked into every page Inline event handlers — any attribute matching on…= (onclick, onsubmit, onload, …) nothing; the forms are plain HTML POSTs and work without JS

auth.css: no expression(, javascript:, vbscript:, url(data:text/html…), and no @import or url() pointing at another origin.

Three implementation details that trip generators:

  • The check runs on HTML-unescaped text. Writing <script> as visible page text still trips the script rule. Do not put these constructs in prose.
  • On a pre-sign-in screen the event-handler pattern is on<word>=, matched anywhere, including in text content. A sentence such as run once = twice matches and rejects the file. Avoid a word beginning with "on" followed directly by =. (This trap does not apply to the four management screens.)
  • Attribute values must be quoted. The required-input check matches name="email" or name='email'; unquoted name=email fails.

On the pre-sign-in screens, no JavaScript at all is the single biggest constraint. Every interaction must be a plain form submit or a link. Client-side validation, password-strength meters, show/hide-password toggles, and AJAX are impossible there. CSS-only interaction (:focus-within, :checked, :has()) is permitted and is the supported way to get interactive behavior.

On the four management screens, write the script inline in the page — a modal, a disclosure panel, a confirm-before-revoke, a client-side filter over the user list are all fine. Those routes also send a Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', connect-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none', img-src 'self' data:), so a remote import() or a fetch() to a third-party origin is blocked by the browser even though no regex inspects the script body. Keep the page working if the script does not run: these are the screens a user manages their own credentials from.

docs.title: 4. Page shell — required, and easy to get wrong
docs.text:
An HTML override replaces the entire document. The framework's layout is not applied around it. Consequences the generator must handle:

  • It must emit a complete document: <!doctype html>, <html>, <head>, <body>. Nothing is added.
  • No stylesheet is linked for you. Emit the links yourself.
  • mark.svg is not injected into an overridden page. The logo override only applies to screens still using the framework page. An override that wants a logo must inline its own SVG (subject to §3's rules) or draw it in CSS.
  • {{message}} and {{error}} are not rendered for you. If the page does not output them, the user never sees "Invitation accepted", "Too many attempts", or "Passwords do not match". Render both on every screen.

Two stylesheet URLs are in the context of every screen:

Variable Points at Use {{default_stylesheet_url}} the framework's auth.css link it first to inherit framework styling, or omit it entirely to start from a blank slate {{stylesheet_url}} your webapp/assets/auth-overrides/auth.css link it last

Required shell (structure only — design is the generator's):

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">
<title>{{title}}</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{stylesheet_url}}">
</head>
<body>
  {{#if error}}<div class="notice error">{{error}}</div>{{/if}}
  {{#if message}}<div class="notice success">{{message}}</div>{{/if}}
  <!-- screen body, per §6 -->
</body>
</html>

noindex,nofollow is on the framework pages and should be kept.

If auth.css is not generated, drop the {{stylesheet_url}} link — otherwise every page load logs a 404 for a file that does not exist.

docs.title: 5. Template language — the available subset
docs.text:
Handlebars (Java, jknack). Available helpers and nothing else:

  • Built-ins: if, unless, each, with, lookup, log
  • Comparison: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, and, or, not

The app-view helpers from server/utils/render.py — select, option, ref_lookup, dateFmt, in, html, session, i18n, get — are deliberately unavailable here. Using one is a compile failure, and the screen falls back.

{{#if registration_open}}<a href="{{register_url}}">Create an account</a>{{/if}}
{{#each users}}<li>{{full_name}} — {{email}}</li>{{/each}}
{{#if (eq status "active")}}…{{/if}}

All output is HTML-escaped. There is no way to emit raw HTML from a value.

docs.title: Common context — present on every screen
docs.text: Variable Type Notes title string the framework's title for the screen message string success notice; "" when none error string error notice; "" when none csrf_token string see below context_path string servlet context path; "" at root default_stylesheet_url string framework auth.css stylesheet_url string your auth.css

docs.title: The two structural requirements
docs.text:
For every screen that has inputs (all except error):

  1. A <form> with an action attribute must appear in the file. Matched as <form … action=…> within one tag.
  2. Every listed input name must appear as name="…", and the literal {{csrf_token}} placeholder must be present. A hardcoded hidden field does not satisfy this — the placeholder is required precisely so that CSRF protection cannot be disabled by a template.

Standard CSRF field for every form:

<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">

The check is a regex over the raw file, so names inside {{#if}} / {{#each}} blocks count as present even if that branch never renders. A screen with two mutually exclusive forms (totp-setup) satisfies the check by containing both.

docs.title: login.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
Required names: email, password, csrf_token

Variable Type Notes action_url string POST target forgot_url string password recovery register_url string only meaningful when registration_open registration_open bool show/hide the register link bootstrap_available bool true when no administrator exists yet; link to {{context_path}}/_soad/auth/bootstrap 
<form method="post" action="{{action_url}}">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">
  <input type="email" name="email" required>
  <input type="password" name="password" required>
  <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
</form>
<a href="{{forgot_url}}">Forgot password?</a>
{{#if registration_open}}<a href="{{register_url}}">Create an account</a>{{/if}}
{{#if bootstrap_available}}
  <a href="{{context_path}}/_soad/auth/bootstrap">Set up the first administrator</a>
{{/if}}

docs.title: verify-totp.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
Shown after a correct password when TOTP is enabled. Credentials are already held in the session; the form carries only the code.

Required names: code, csrf_token Context: action_url

docs.title: register.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
Only reachable when open registration is enabled.

Required names: full_name, email, password, password_confirm, csrf_token Context: action_url, login_url

docs.title: bootstrap.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
First-administrator setup; reachable only while no active administrator exists.

Required names: full_name, email, password, password_confirm, csrf_token Context: action_url, login_url, password_min_length (integer, currently 10)

Use minlength="{{password_min_length}}" on both password inputs.

docs.title: forgot.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
One template serves both the empty form and the post-submit confirmation; branch on submitted.

Required names: email, csrf_token Context: action_url, login_url, submitted (bool)

The response is deliberately generic — it does not reveal whether the account exists. Do not word the confirmation as though it does.

docs.title: reset.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
Required names: token, password, password_confirm, csrf_token Context: action_url, token, login_url, password_min_length

token must be carried through as a hidden field:

<input type="hidden" name="token" value="{{token}}">

docs.title: invite.html — POST {{action_url}}
docs.text:
Invitation acceptance / initial password. Identical shape to reset.html; a separate file so the wording can differ.

Required names: token, password, password_confirm, csrf_token Context: action_url, token, login_url, password_min_length

The four screens that follow — profile, sessions, totp-setup, admin-users — are the signed-in management screens. They are the only ones that accept an inline <script> and inline event handlers (see §3), and the only ones that get the wide card. error, after them, is back to the pre-sign-in rules.

Shared shell context — on all four, so the same nav, sign-out link, and "signed in as" can be pasted into each:

Variable Type Notes profile_url, sessions_url, totp_setup_url, admin_users_url string navigation logout_url string plain link; the CSRF token is already in the query string, so a template cannot build this itself user object id, email, full_name, status

{{admin_users_url}} is present for every user; non-administrators get 403 on that page. Hide it or accept the 403 — there is no "is admin" flag here.

docs.title: profile.html — two forms
docs.text:
Required names: full_name, current_password, password, password_confirm, csrf_token

Variable Type Notes action_url string POST — profile update (full_name) password_action_url string POST — password change

Two separate forms are required — one to {{action_url}} with full_name, one to {{password_action_url}} with current_password + password + password_confirm. Each needs its own CSRF field.

docs.title: sessions.html — POST {{revoke_action_url}} per row
docs.text:
Required names: session_id, csrf_token

Variable Type Notes revoke_action_url string POST target sessions array see below

Each entry of sessions: id, created_at, last_seen_at, user_agent, ip_address — all strings, pre-defaulted ("Unknown client", "unknown address"), newest first.

Each row needs its own form; there is no bulk revoke endpoint.

{{#each sessions}}
  <li>
    {{user_agent}} — {{ip_address}} — {{last_seen_at}}
    <form method="post" action="{{../revoke_action_url}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{../csrf_token}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="session_id" value="{{id}}">
      <button type="submit">Revoke</button>
    </form>
  </li>
{{/each}}

Note the ../ prefix inside {{#each}}. The validator's {{csrf_token}} check is satisfied by the shell's plain {{csrf_token}}, but each form still needs the ../-qualified value to actually render — so include at least one bare {{csrf_token}} outside the loop if every form is inside one.

docs.title: totp-setup.html — two mutually exclusive states
docs.text:
Required names: code, current_password, csrf_token — all three must be in the file even though only one state renders at a time.

Variable Type Notes enabled bool branch on this secret string base32 secret; "" when already enabled qr_data_url string data:image/… for <img src="…">; "" when enabled setup_action_url string POST — enable (field code) disable_action_url string POST — disable (field current_password)

{{qr_data_url}} in an src attribute is allowed — only data:text/html is blocked, image data URLs are fine. Show {{secret}} as text too, for users who cannot scan.

{{#if enabled}}
  <form method="post" action="{{disable_action_url}}">
    <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">
    <input type="password" name="current_password" required>
    <button type="submit">Disable</button>
  </form>
{{else}}
  <img alt="TOTP QR code" src="{{qr_data_url}}">
  <code>{{secret}}</code>
  <form method="post" action="{{setup_action_url}}">
    <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">
    <input name="code" inputmode="numeric" required>
    <button type="submit">Enable</button>
  </form>
{{/if}}

docs.title: admin-users.html — four POST targets
docs.text:
The most demanding screen. Required names: email, user_id, role_code, operation, status, csrf_token — all six, even for a minimal page.

Variable Type Notes create_action_url string POST — add user invite_action_url string POST — (re-)send setup link; field email role_action_url string POST — grant/remove role status_action_url string POST — enable/disable users array see below roles array { code, name } form object re-populates the add-user form after a validation error: full_name, email, role_codes (array) invite_link string one-time setup link, "" when none invitation_created bool true only on the invite-result render, where users and roles are empty

Each entry of users: id, email, full_name, status, pending (bool), roles (array of role-code strings), next_status (the value to post to flip enabled/disabled).

pending means the account exists but has no password — it cannot sign in until the setup link is followed. Render it distinctly from active.

The four operations:

{{! 1. add user — role_codes is a repeated checkbox, name is PLURAL here }}
<form method="post" action="{{create_action_url}}">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{csrf_token}}">
  <input name="full_name" value="{{form.full_name}}" required>
  <input type="email" name="email" value="{{form.email}}" required>
  {{#each roles}}
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="role_codes" value="{{code}}"> {{name}}</label>
  {{/each}}
  <input type="password" name="password" minlength="10">
  <input type="password" name="password_confirm" minlength="10">
  <button type="submit">Create user</button>
</form>
{{! leaving both password fields empty creates a pending account + setup link }}

{{#if invite_link}}<p><a href="{{invite_link}}">{{invite_link}}</a></p>{{/if}}

{{#each users}}
  <li>
    {{full_name}} — {{email}} — {{#if pending}}pending{{else}}{{status}}{{/if}}
    {{#each roles}}<span>{{this}}</span>{{/each}}

    {{! 2. grant/remove a role — role_code is SINGULAR here }}
    <form method="post" action="{{../role_action_url}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{../csrf_token}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="user_id" value="{{id}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="operation" value="grant">
      <select name="role_code">
        {{#each ../roles}}<option value="{{code}}">{{name}}</option>{{/each}}
      </select>
      <button type="submit">Grant</button>
    </form>

    {{! 3. enable/disable }}
    <form method="post" action="{{../status_action_url}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{../csrf_token}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="user_id" value="{{id}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="status" value="{{next_status}}">
      <button type="submit">{{#if (eq status "active")}}Disable{{else}}Enable{{/if}}</button>
    </form>

    {{! 4. re-send setup link — only useful for pending accounts }}
    {{#if pending}}
    <form method="post" action="{{../invite_action_url}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{../csrf_token}}">
      <input type="hidden" name="email" value="{{email}}">
      <button type="submit">Re-send setup link</button>
    </form>
    {{/if}}
  </li>
{{/each}}

Watch the two role field names: role_codes (plural, checkboxes, create form) and role_code (singular, select, grant/remove). Only the singular one is required by the validator; the plural create-form fields are optional — a template that omits them keeps validating and simply does not offer that feature. To remove a role, post operation = remove instead of grant.

{{invite_link}} must be shown when non-empty: with SMTP unconfigured it is the only way the administrator can deliver the setup link.

docs.title: error.html — no form
docs.text:
Used for every failure response: 400, 403 (CSRF mismatch, non-admin), 404 (disabled feature, unknown page), 500, 503 (schema/manifest not ready).

Required names: none. No form or CSRF needed.

Variable Type Notes status integer HTTP status error string the message; also in {{error}}

The HTTP status code is preserved regardless of what the template renders. Keep the message generic — it is shown to unauthenticated visitors.

docs.title: 7. auth.css
docs.text:
Path: webapp/assets/auth-overrides/auth.css, served at {{stylesheet_url}} (= <context>/assets/auth-overrides/auth.css).

  • Rejected: expression(, javascript:, vbscript:, url(data:text/html…), and any @import or url() pointing at another origin (https://, http://, //host).
  • Limit 256 KiB.
  • Self-contained. There is no second file, no image, no font file — the folder recognizes only the names in §1. Embed any image or font as a data: URI (image/font types are fine; only data:text/html is blocked). Do not @import or reference a CDN: these pages are built for air-gapped deployments, and a fetch that fails leaves the login screen unstyled.
  • If the generator emits full-page HTML overrides with self-contained class names, it does not need to link {{default_stylesheet_url}}, and the framework class names below are irrelevant.
  • If the generator overrides only some screens, the non-overridden ones still render with the framework layout, which links the framework stylesheet and then yours. In that case auth.css is a cascade layer over the defaults, and these are the framework's hooks:

.auth-card / .auth-card.wide, .auth-mark, .auth-body, .notice, .notice.error, .notice.success, nav.tab-bar, .row-main, .row-identity, .row-sub, .row-roles, .row-actions, .badge, .badge-active, .badge-disabled, .badge-pending, .chip, .chip-remove, .inline, .form-hint, .link-box, .role-picker, .role-option.

.wide is applied to profile, sessions, totp-setup, and admin-users; the other screens are the narrow centered card.

Recommended: for a consistent result, generate either all 12 HTML files, or none of them plus auth.css only. A partial HTML set means overridden and framework screens sit side by side in the same flow.

docs.title: 8. mark.svg (optional logo)
docs.text:
Path: webapp/WEB-INF/auth-overrides/mark.svg.

This only affects screens rendered by the framework layout. An overridden HTML page does not receive it — inline the logo in that page's own markup instead. It is worth generating only when shipping auth.css without HTML overrides.

Not a Handlebars template — inlined verbatim. Its rules:

  • The whole file is one <svg>…</svg> element. No <?xml?>, no <!DOCTYPE>, no <!ENTITY>, nothing before or after the root tag.
  • No <script>, no on…= handlers, no <iframe>/<object>/<embed>/ <foreignObject>.
  • href/xlink:href may only be a local #fragment (e.g. <use> referencing a <symbol> in the same file). No external file, no data: URL.
  • Build from shape elements: <svg>, <g>, <path>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <rect>, <polygon>, <use>.
  • 24 KiB limit.
  • Set a viewBox; omit width/height. Any class or aria-hidden on the root is stripped and replaced with class="auth-mark" aria-hidden="true", so sizing comes from CSS.
  • Shown on the narrow screens only (login, register, forgot, reset, invite, verify-2FA, error). Wide management screens never show it.

docs.title: 9. Generator checklist
docs.text:
Per HTML file:

  • [ ] Complete document: doctype, <html>, <head>, <body>
  • [ ] <title>{{title}}</title> and the {{stylesheet_url}} link (only if auth.css is generated)
  • [ ] Both {{message}} and {{error}} rendered
  • [ ] Every required input name from §6, quoted: name="email"
  • [ ] A literal {{csrf_token}} placeholder, plus a CSRF hidden field in every form (../csrf_token inside {{#each}})
  • [ ] Every form has an action attribute pointing at the screen's *_action_url
  • [ ] No {{{…}}}, and no <script src=…> or <script type="module"> anywhere
  • [ ] On a pre-sign-in screen: no <script> at all and no on…= attribute (check prose text too). On profile / sessions / totp-setup / admin-users: inline script and handlers are fine
  • [ ] Only the §5 helpers used
  • [ ] Under 128 KiB, UTF-8

Per output set:

  • [ ] auth.css at webapp/assets/auth-overrides/, not WEB-INF/
  • [ ] No files other than the names in §1
  • [ ] No external URL anywhere — no CDN, font host, or remote image. This is enforced, not advisory: an https://, http://, or //host URL in href/src/action/formaction, or in a CSS @import/url(), rejects the file

Verification after copying in: load each route below and confirm the page is yours, not the framework's. A framework-looking page means the file was rejected — the server log names the screen and the reason.

GET  /_soad/auth/login          → login.html
POST /_soad/auth/login          → verify-totp.html (TOTP users)
GET  /_soad/auth/register       → register.html      (open registration only)
GET  /_soad/auth/bootstrap      → bootstrap.html     (no admin yet)
GET  /_soad/auth/forgot         → forgot.html
GET  /_soad/auth/reset?token=…  → reset.html
GET  /_soad/auth/invite?token=… → invite.html
GET  /_soad/auth/profile        → profile.html
GET  /_soad/auth/sessions       → sessions.html
GET  /_soad/auth/totp/setup     → totp-setup.html
GET  /_soad/auth/admin/users    → admin-users.html
GET  /_soad/auth/nonexistent    → error.html (404)
GET  /_soad/auth/health         → readiness JSON (not overridable)

docs.title: 10. Scope
docs.text: An override changes presentation only. It cannot change credential verification, session handling, CSRF, roles, permissions, rate limiting, or token lifetimes, and it cannot add or remove a route. For different authentication behavior, use a custom provider instead.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Properties are loaded from SUFIA_HOME/conf/sufia.properties; environment variables overlay them. The normal mapping replaces underscores with dots: db_default_driver_class becomes db.default.driver.class. Use the documented spelling rather than inventing an alias.

The development profile is app/conf/sufia.properties; application-only images copy app/conf/sufia-runtime.properties into that runtime location. Do not copy environment-specific values from the development profile into docs or releases. Restart for configuration changes unless a feature explicitly documents live updates.

docs.title: Application and database
docs.text:
Property Environment Meaning sufia.home SUFIA_HOME Runtime root; special startup variable sufia.mode sufia_mode development reloads transaction modules; production for deployments sufia.context_path sufia_context_path Servlet context; special compatibility handling sufia.app.name sufia_app_name Application display name for runtime pages/email sufia.hostname sufia_hostname Public origin used for generated links sufia.welcome.transaction sufia_welcome_transaction Operator override for root welcome transaction db.default.url db_default_url JDBC URL for default app db.default.driver.class db_default_driver_class JDBC driver, e.g. com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver db.default.username db_default_username Database account db.default.password db_default_password Database password, injected as a secret

The driver reader also accepts legacy driverclass/driver_class spellings, but examples use driver.class. Each configured datasource name is also an application name. Do not assume the single-app local-auth manifest architecture provides arbitrary multi-tenant security automatically.

Welcome resolution is the operator property first, then the released WEB-INF/sufia-app.properties, then the framework fallback. An explicit blank operator value selects the existing static index instead of a transaction.

docs.title: Sessions and uploads
docs.text:
Property Shipped production value / behavior session.cookie.httponly true session.cookie.secure true; use HTTPS session.cookie.samesite NONE; tracker examples override to LAX session.timeout 1800 seconds servlet idle timeout max.file.upload.size Maximum individual upload bytes; legacy maxfileuploadsize takes precedence if set max.request.upload.size Aggregate request bytes; legacy maxrequestuploadsize takes precedence file.upload.temp.dir Upload spool directory; otherwise JVM tmp/soad-uploads

Environment forms include session_cookie_secure, session_cookie_samesite, session_timeout, and max_file_upload_size. Check whether a legacy upload property is already set before adding a dotted replacement. Application auth records have their own expiry and revocation checks. Jetty's file session store uses JVM tmp/s0-session-store.

docs.title: Email and AI
docs.text:
SMTP: mail.smtp.host, mail.smtp.port, mail.smtp.username, mail.smtp.password, mail.sender.email. The corresponding variables replace dots with underscores. Read the current TLS limitation in the integration chapter.

AI: ai.enabled, ai.provider, ai.endpoint, ai.api.key, ai.model, ai.auto.accept. IDE-saved fields take precedence over properties/environment. ai.one.shot.auto.security defaults true; turning it off changes inference, not explicit requests for protected access.

For generation limits inspect app/s0adm/ai/config.py for ai.turn.cap, ai.one.shot.turn.cap, ai.context.max.tokens, and ai.max.output.tokens; tune against the selected provider's actual limits. These are development/IDE settings, not runtime application requirements.

docs.title: Advanced runtime mappings
docs.text:
Servlet/filter mappings are configured as servlet.<name>.mapping/file and filter.<name>.mapping/file. Ordinary application transactions need no per-route configuration. Static mappings use static.<name>.mapping/dir. Context listeners use the configured listener mechanism.

Error overrides use error.page.<status> and error.page_exception; see error pages. The development-only manifest exemption setting sufia.security.manifest.exempt_apps exists for the IDE; do not exempt your protected application to silence a setup error.

docs.title: Error page reference
docs.text:
The runtime bundles three generic HTML pages in app/server/errors/. They use /assets/soad-auth/auth.css, include a context-aware home link, and never display exception messages or stack traces. Responses use UTF-8 and Cache-Control: no-store.

Error Transaction override Class Conventional template 404 (including missing resources and transactions) default/errors/err404.py Err404 errors/_err404/err404.html Explicit sendError(500) default/errors/err500.py Err500 errors/_err500/err500.html Uncaught exception (HTTP 500) default/errors/errexc.py Errexc errors/_errexc/errexc.html

Paths are relative to app/webapp/WEB-INF/jython/; template paths are relative to its default/ directory. Include __init__.py in default/ and default/errors/ when creating the files manually. Each override is optional and discovered independently. Default-app overrides handle application requests, including other application names. IDE (/s0adm, /assets/s0adm), internal /_soad and /logs errors always use bundled pages.

docs.title: Conventional views
docs.text:
For example, create default/errors/err404.py:

class Err404:
    def view(self, ctx):
        ctx.output['heading'] = 'This page is no longer available'
        ctx.output['home_url'] = ctx.getCtxPath() + '/'

Create default/errors/_err404/err404.html:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Page not found</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ctxPath}}/assets/soad-auth/auth.css">
</head>
<body>
  <main class="auth-card auth-body">
    <h1>{{heading}}</h1>
    <p>Please return home to continue.</p>
    <a class="auth-button" href="{{home_url}}">Go home</a>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

Only view(ctx) runs: no automatic database connection or transaction, authentication check, application filter, routed action, or page-layout hook. ctx.output and ctxPath work as usual. Any database access explicitly added by an override is its responsibility and may fail during an outage.

docs.title: Callable rendering
docs.text:
An explicit 500 override can reuse a named template. Create default/errors/err500.py:

from utils import render

class Err500:
    def view(self, ctx):
        ctx.output['heading'] = 'Please try again later'
        ctx.output['home_url'] = ctx.getCtxPath() + '/'
        ctx.go_to = render.as_view(ctx, 'err404', group='errors', code='err404')

This uses the complete template above. Any callable ctx.go_to is supported; its returned text is written to the buffered response. It may instead write to ctx.getResponse() and return None. A renderer setting status 200 does not change the original 404 or 500 status. Output is published as UTF-8 HTML; override headers, cookies and content types are not published.

Redirects (including string ctx.go_to) and secondary sendError calls fail the override. Output, including flushed output, is buffered and discarded on failure. The failure is logged and the matching bundled page is used. If the bundled page also fails, the runtime emits minimal generic HTML. Recursive dispatch is rejected. A response already committed before error handling cannot be replaced.

docs.title: Explicit disclosure of error details
docs.text:
ctx.getError() returns None outside the dedicated error dispatch. During it, it returns the captured original error map:

  • status: original HTTP status (500 for exceptions).
  • kind: err404, err500, or errexc.
  • message: servlet error message, possibly None.
  • request_uri: original request URI, including the context path.
  • exception: Java/Jython exception object, or None.
  • stack_trace: preserved runtime Jython traceback followed by the Java stack when an exception exists; an empty string for responses without an exception.

The map is not automatically included in template data. To opt in, create default/errors/errexc.py:

from webgeaz.sufia.core import Application


def should_show_details(ctx):
    # Example policy: deliberately opt in only on a private development server.
    return (Application.getProperty('sufia.mode') == 'development'
            and Application.getProperty('errors.show_details') == 'true')


class Errexc:
    def view(self, ctx):
        error = ctx.getError()
        ctx.output['show_stack'] = should_show_details(ctx)
        if ctx.output['show_stack']:
            ctx.output['stack_trace'] = error['stack_trace']

Create default/errors/_errexc/errexc.html:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Request failed</title></head>
<body>
  <h1>Something went wrong</h1>
  <a href="{{ctxPath}}/">Go home</a>
  {{#if show_stack}}<pre>{{stack_trace}}</pre>{{/if}}
</body>
</html>

Use escaped {{stack_trace}}, never triple braces. Exception messages may contain user-controlled text. The disclosure policy belongs entirely to override code; the runtime never enables it automatically, even in development.

docs.title: Configuration and rollout
docs.text:
Existing error.page.<status> settings replace the corresponding status mapping. error.page_exception replaces the uncaught-exception mapping. Exception routing is separate from explicit 500 routing; configure error.page_exception to replace the exception page. Explicit configured pages retain their existing servlet lifecycle; the dedicated lifecycle described above applies to the built-in route.

Rebuild the runtime (./dev.sh build) and restart to install the Java changes. Deploy server/ErrorViews.py, server/errors/, and the updated auth stylesheet with the runtime. Restart after changing error mappings or production override code. In sufia.mode=development, overrides reload on each error request, following transaction conventions. Bundled HTML is read on each error. No migration is needed. Existing PDF rendering error handling is unchanged.

docs.title: Database migrations and older installations
docs.text: There are two separate database lifecycles: S0ADM's control-plane schema and your application's business/auth schema. Choose the intended database before running any SQL.

docs.title: Existing S0ADM installations
docs.text:
New IDE databases are initialized from app/s0adm/setupdb-s0adm.sql when empty. An existing database is not rebuilt by restarting an image. Review the numbered SQL files under app/migrations/ against your installed columns and migration history:

File Feature 001_ai_chat.sql AI conversations 002_user_2fa.sql IDE second-factor fields 003_user_avatar.sql Profile avatar 004_app_security.sql Application security metadata 005_custom_auth_provider.sql Provider selection 006_ai_provider_settings.sql IDE AI provider settings 007_security_rationale_length.sql Expanded rationale 008_ai_auto_accept.sql AI auto-accept setting 009_user_ui_theme.sql User theme preference

Back up before changes. The migration files are not a promise that every SQL dialect accepts every statement or that an already-applied file can be rerun. For local H2 using dev.sh, stop the app before migrate:

./dev.sh stop
./dev.sh migrate app/migrations/002_user_2fa.sql
./dev.sh start

Use the appropriate unapplied migration, not necessarily 002. Check the script's database target. External H2 access while a process is running requires compatible AUTO_SERVER settings; stopping the local process avoids file-lock ambiguity. For MySQL use your normal reviewed migration client.

The historical README's 2FA guidance has been consolidated here. Its key requirement remains: existing installs need the schema update and refreshed models, not just new application files.

docs.title: Application migrations
docs.text:
Keep ordered, version-controlled business SQL in your application project. The tracker initial schema is for a fresh database; evolve it using new migrations rather than editing and replaying the initial script.

Local-auth generation produces auth-mysql.sql and auth-h2.sql beside the security manifest. Install the bundle for your dialect. The manifest checksum must match installed metadata; changing roles/permissions requires compatible metadata deployment, not just controller edits.

Auth bundles contain schema/role/permission metadata, not users or secrets. Review grant changes because reinstalling metadata can change effective access. Back up user/session data separately.

docs.title: Deployment order
docs.text:
1. Back up and confirm the target database.
  2. Apply reviewed auth/business migrations.
  3. Start the matching image so models regenerate.
  4. Check auth health and application behavior.

Rollback must pair a compatible image, manifest, and database state. MySQL DDL may commit implicitly; a failed migration is not necessarily automatically undone.

docs.title: Rendering and utility reference
docs.text: Import from utils import render. Most rendering functions return a callable: assign it to ctx.go_to. Set ctx.page_layout=False for non-page responses.

docs.title: Renderers
docs.text:
Call Result / important parameters as_view(ctx, view, group=None, code=None, loc=None, file=None, combine_map=None) Handlebars HTML; view name omits .html; sets status 200 as_string_template(ctx, view) Inline Handlebars string rendered from output as_json(ctx, obj=None, status=200) JSON; omitted obj serializes all output as_html(ctx, code=None, loc=None) Reads raw HTML without template expansion as_string(ctx, text_string, status=200) Literal HTML string, not escaped text as_file(ctx, file, content_type, filename=None, attachment=True) Streams a filesystem path or java.io.File as_blob(ctx, content, content_type, filename, attachment=False) Streams byte content as_pdf(ctx, view, group=None, code=None, file=None, filename=None, combine_map=None, attachment=False) Converts a Handlebars document to PDF

Examples:

ctx.go_to = render.as_view(ctx, "edit")
ctx.go_to = render.as_view(ctx, "summary", group="reports", code="monthly")
ctx.go_to = render.as_json(ctx, {"ok": True}, status=201)
ctx.go_to = render.as_blob(ctx, data, "application/octet-stream",
                          "report.bin", attachment=True)

These lines are alternatives; only the last assigned response is used. Some JDBC drivers return a java.sql.Blob rather than bytes. For deliberately bounded blobs, call blob.getBytes(1, int(blob.length())) before as_blob; its input must support byte-array operations. Stream large values separately. Avoid loc/file unless intentionally resolving a framework-specific alternate view location. Never let a submitted path select an arbitrary template/download. as_string is HTML, so use constant text or explicit escaping for user values.

docs.title: Template helpers
docs.text:
Helper Example / purpose eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte {{#eq status "done"}}Complete{{/eq}} and, or, not Conditional composition length, size {{length projects}} for collections dateFmt {{dateFmt created_date "yyyy-MM-dd"}} html Escape text, preserve newlines, linkify URLs select, option Build select markup/options from supplied refs or a model table ref_lookup Resolve a display label by model table or supplied refs session Read a named session attribute; do not expose secrets get Resolve an output key as safe content; use only trusted values i18n Resolve resource-bundle labels

The normal view renderer also registers Handlebars string helpers. Model-backed select/ref helpers can perform database queries. Prefer prefiltered refs for private data so the helper cannot accidentally show a global table:

{{select name="assignee_id" refs=people label="full_name" value="id" selected=task.assignee_id}}

Do not put untrusted SQL in a helper's filter attribute. For reusable views, prepare lookup lists in the controller to avoid per-row queries.

docs.title: Email and Java libraries
docs.text:
The SMTP entrypoint is:

from utils import mailer
mailer.send(None, "recipient@example.com", "Project update",
            "Your project was updated.", html=False)

Its full signature is send(fr, to, subject, content, cc=[], bcc=[], html=False, attachment=[], inline=[], reply_to=None). Use actual configured recipients and reviewed templates. send_api is a separate provider-specific path; inspect its configured API integration before adopting it. See email deployment constraints.

Bundled libraries include Java time/IO, Google Guava, Apache Commons, Apache POI, Jakarta Mail, and the PDF converter. The authoritative versions are in sufiao-core/build.gradle; do not infer that any arbitrary Java JAR is already bundled.

Log through from sufia.util import Log and Log.info(ctx, message). Use utils.fileupload.UploadedFile for multipart file handling rather than calling a second upload parser.

docs.title: Transaction filter reference
docs.text:
Transaction filters let an application run reusable request and response logic around the normal servlet pipeline. They are useful for concerns such as request logging, response headers, maintenance gates, correlation IDs, and other logic that must run before or after a request reaches a servlet.

SØAD implements this feature with one framework filter mapped to /*. The framework filter discovers transaction classes in the reserved filter group and presents each one as a servlet-style filter.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Create a transaction named filter/request_logger:

webapp/WEB-INF/jython/default/
├── __init__.py
└── filter/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── request_logger.py

Define all three lifecycle methods in request_logger.py:

from java.util.logging import Level, Logger


logger = Logger.getLogger("filter.request_logger")


class Request_logger(object):
    url_mapping = "/*"

    def filter_init(self, config):
        logger.log(Level.INFO, "Request logger initialized")

    def do_filter(self, request, response, chain):
        logger.log(Level.INFO, "Request: %s" % request.getRequestURI())
        chain.doFilter(request, response)

    def destroy(self):
        logger.log(Level.INFO, "Request logger destroyed")

Restart or redeploy the server after creating, deleting, renaming, or changing a transaction filter. Discovery and transaction instances are cached for the lifetime of the framework filter.

docs.title: Required contract
docs.text:
A Python file qualifies as a transaction filter when all of the following are true:

  • It is directly under webapp/WEB-INF/jython/default/filter/.
  • Its filename is a valid transaction code, for example request_logger.py.
  • It declares the conventional transaction class. The filename request_logger.py maps to the class Request_logger.
  • The class implements filter_init, do_filter, and destroy with the signatures described below.
class Example(object):
    url_mapping = "/*"

    def filter_init(self, config):
        pass

    def do_filter(self, request, response, chain):
        chain.doFilter(request, response)

    def destroy(self):
        pass

The filter group is reserved for this contract. A filter transaction is not a normal MVC endpoint: do not add view(ctx), a Handlebars view directory, or an ACCESS_POLICY merely to make it look like a routed transaction.

docs.title: filter_init(config)
docs.text:
The framework calls filter_init once after constructing the filter. config is the jakarta.servlet.FilterConfig of the framework dispatcher and provides access to the servlet context and configured initialization parameters.

Use this method for immutable setup that can be shared safely across requests. If it raises an exception, filter initialization fails and the error is allowed to propagate to the servlet container.

docs.title: do_filter(request, response, chain)
docs.text:
The framework calls do_filter for every request that matches the transaction's URL mapping. The arguments are the current servlet request, servlet response, and continuation chain.

Call chain.doFilter(request, response) exactly once to continue to the next matching transaction filter and eventually the requested servlet. Code before that call is pre-processing; code after it is post-processing:

class Timing(object):
    def filter_init(self, config):
        pass

    def do_filter(self, request, response, chain):
        started = System.nanoTime()
        try:
            chain.doFilter(request, response)
        finally:
            elapsed = System.nanoTime() - started
            # Record elapsed here.

    def destroy(self):
        pass

Import System from java.lang when using the timing example.

A filter may intentionally omit the chain call to short-circuit the request. When it does, it must complete the response itself:

class Maintenance(object):
    url_mapping = "/t/admin/*"

    def filter_init(self, config):
        pass

    def do_filter(self, request, response, chain):
        if request.getHeader("X-Maintenance-Bypass") is None:
            response.sendError(503, "Service temporarily unavailable")
            return
        chain.doFilter(request, response)

    def destroy(self):
        pass

Do not catch and suppress downstream errors unless the filter has a documented recovery policy. An exception raised by a transaction filter, a later filter, or the target servlet propagates with normal servlet-filter behavior.

docs.title: destroy()
docs.text: The framework calls destroy during shutdown or filter replacement. Release resources created by filter_init here. Filters are destroyed in reverse initialization order. Destruction failures are not silently converted into successful shutdowns.

docs.title: URL mappings
docs.text:
Declare an optional class-level url_mapping. It may be one string or a list of strings. When it is absent, the mapping defaults to /*.

class Api_headers(object):
    url_mapping = ["/t/api/*", "*.json"]

    def filter_init(self, config):
        pass

    def do_filter(self, request, response, chain):
        response.setHeader("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
        chain.doFilter(request, response)

    def destroy(self):
        pass

Mappings follow servlet URL-pattern conventions:

Pattern Matches /* Every request /health Only the exact /health path /t/api/* /t/api and paths below it *.json Any request path ending in .json

Patterns are matched against the request path relative to the servlet context. The query string is not part of the match. A list matches when any one of its patterns matches. An empty value, unsupported pattern, or non-string list item is a configuration error and fails initialization.

The transaction mapping decides whether that transaction is invoked; it does not register another container filter. The single framework dispatcher remains mapped to /*.

docs.title: Discovery, order, and application scope
docs.text:
The dispatcher scans only the default/filter package. These filters are deployment-wide and may therefore see requests for named applications, built-in authentication routes, static resources, and other servlets. Always narrow url_mapping when a filter should affect only part of the server.

Eligible filters are initialized and invoked in ascending alphabetical order by transaction code. For deliberate ordering, use descriptive prefixes that still follow transaction naming rules:

filter/a_request_id.py
filter/b_request_log.py
filter/c_response_headers.py

Only filters whose mapping matches the current request enter that request's chain. Post-processing runs in the reverse order naturally as nested chain calls return.

Discovery happens during dispatcher initialization and is cached. A server restart or redeployment is required after adding, removing, or renaming a filter and after changing filter code or mappings.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
The filter group is tolerant of incomplete transaction files but strict once a filter qualifies:

Condition Behavior One or more required lifecycle methods are missing Skip the transaction and log a warning Module import or class construction fails Fail initialization and propagate the error url_mapping is invalid Fail initialization and propagate the error filter_init fails Fail initialization and propagate the error do_filter or downstream processing fails Propagate the request error destroy fails Report the destruction error

Skipping an incomplete class supports ordinary files being inspected while they are being created, but it can also hide an intended security filter. Check the server log after deployment and test security-sensitive filters explicitly.

docs.title: Runtime and concurrency rules
docs.text:
Transaction filter instances follow servlet-filter singleton semantics. One cached instance may serve many requests concurrently.

  • Do not store request-specific data on self.
  • Prefer local variables and request attributes for per-request state.
  • Make shared mutable state thread-safe.
  • Keep filter_init setup immutable where possible.
  • Do not assume a WebContext, ActiveJDBC connection, or database transaction.
  • Do not assume the request is a /t/... transaction request.
  • Do not write a response after it has been committed by downstream processing.

The arguments to do_filter are raw servlet objects. If a filter needs a value later in the request pipeline, attach it to the request:

request.setAttribute("correlation_id", correlation_id)

docs.title: Default framework registration
docs.text:
The framework dispatcher is enabled in both development and production runtime profiles with:

filter.transaction_filter.mapping = /*
filter.transaction_filter.file = server/TransactionFilter.py

Applications normally do not need to add these properties themselves. If a custom runtime configuration replaces the supplied sufia.properties, retain both entries to keep transaction-filter support enabled.

docs.title: AI agent generation rules
docs.text:
When an AI agent creates or edits a transaction in the filter group, it must apply the following rules:

  1. Treat filter as the reserved deployment-wide transaction-filter group.
  2. Generate one controller file and no view templates unless the developer explicitly requests unrelated files.
  3. Generate the conventional capitalized class with all three methods: filter_init(config), do_filter(request, response, chain), and destroy().
  4. Do not generate view(ctx) or ACCESS_POLICY for the filter contract.
  5. Declare url_mapping only when needed; otherwise rely on the /* default.
  6. Call chain.doFilter(request, response) exactly once for normal continuation, or intentionally complete the response and return for a short circuit.
  7. Preserve servlet exception behavior; do not add a blanket exception handler that hides failures.
  8. Keep the instance thread-safe and do not place request state on self.
  9. Tell the developer that a restart or redeployment is required for the change to be discovered.

Before proposing a filter, the agent should state its transaction code, URL mapping, whether it continues or short-circuits the chain, and any shared state created during initialization.

docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
• The file is under default/filter and its class name matches its filename.
  • All three lifecycle methods use the exact required signatures.
  • The mapping is absent, a valid string, or a valid list of strings.
  • The chain is called exactly once on every continuation path.
  • Every short-circuit path completes the response.
  • Exceptions are allowed to propagate unless recovery is intentional.
  • Shared state is safe for concurrent requests.
  • The mapping is narrow enough for deployment-wide scope.
  • Deployment includes a server restart or redeployment.

docs.text:

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Transaction A group/code Jython controller and its views Action A routed public method, normally view/save/edit Database transaction Commit/rollback boundary around request work WebContext / ctx Request/response bridge and template output map Model Generated ActiveJDBC class for a database table/view Introspect Regenerate model metadata/classes from database schema S0ADM Browser IDE and development control plane Runtime Application-serving process/container Security profile Public, authenticated, or mixed application classification Auth mode Local, custom, or public identity implementation ACCESS_POLICY Controller mapping from action names to access requirements Permission Registered capability granted through roles Ownership Business rule restricting which records a user may access Manifest Versioned application security metadata with checksum Release Source/image artifact; not a database backup Skill Instructions/reference bundle loaded by a compatible coding agent
